title.value: Double-Linear Thompson Sampling for Context-Attentive Bandits
title.justification: The paper introduces a novel algorithm, Context-Attentive Thompson Sampling (CATS), and is focused on the context-attentive bandit framework, which justifies this title as it encompasses the core contribution and focus of the research.
title.quote: In this paper, we analyze and extend an online learning framework known as Context-Attentive Bandit, and derive a novel algorithm, called Context-Attentive Thompson Sampling (CATS).

analysis.description: This paper generalizes the Context-Attentive Bandit (CAB) framework by proposing a novel algorithm called Context-Attentive Thompson Sampling (CATS). The research extends the CAB setting where not all context variables are observed initially, allowing the agent to select additional variables. The paper provides theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations demonstrating the effectiveness of CATS over traditional methods across several datasets in both stationary and non-stationary environments.

type.justification: The paper presents both theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations, comparing the proposed CATS algorithm's performance with other methods across various datasets, indicating an empirical study focus.
type.quote: We provide a theoretical regret analysis and an extensive empirical evaluation demonstrating advantages of the proposed approach over several baseline methods on a variety of real-life datasets.

name.justification: The research is centered on the Context-Attentive Bandit (CAB) framework, which is a specialized area within Reinforcement Learning as it involves decision-making with partial observations and context-attentive mechanisms.
name.quote: The contextual bandit problem is a variant of the extensively studied multi-armed bandit problem...where at each iteration, the agent observes an N -dimensional context (feature vector) and uses it, along with the rewards of the arms played in the past, to decide which arm to play.

name.justification: The techniques and algorithms discussed, such as Thompson Sampling adaptations and bandit problems, fall under the broad umbrella of Machine Learning.
name.quote: The contextual bandit (CB) problem has been extensively studied in the past, and a variety of solutions have been proposed.

name.justification: The context-attentive bandit problem aligns with online learning as it requires the algorithm to learn and make decisions sequentially over time.
name.quote: We analyze and extend an online learning framework known as Context-Attentive Bandit.

name.justification: The paper introduces CATS as a novel algorithm derived for the proposed problem setup in context-attentive bandits.
name.quote: We derive a novel algorithm, called Context-Attentive Thompson Sampling (CATS), which builds upon the Linear Thompson Sampling approach.

is_contributed.justification: CATS is the main contribution of the paper, extending existing algorithms to suit the context-attentive setting.
is_contributed.quote: We derive a novel algorithm, called Context-Attentive Thompson Sampling (CATS).

is_executed.justification: The paper does not specify the execution environment (GPU or CPU) for the model, focusing instead on theoretical and comparative evaluation.

is_compared.justification: The paper includes comparative results of CATS with other models across multiple datasets, emphasizing its performance advantages.
is_compared.quote: We compare the proposed CATS algorithm with...Thompson Sampling with Restricted Context (TSRC) and several others.
